statement: In the above setting the following statements hold. (i) The discrepancy of (X, H) at (P, y) is a(P), and its discrepancy at a pure weight is zero. Thus a(P) is a nonnegative integer for every primitive P, and u ∈ int C. (ii) For rational µ ∈ int C, the ray quotient Vµ is normal and projective, with function field K. The order function L(µ)(P) = min y∈∆P ⟨y, µ⟩ (D.5) is the b-pullback of an ample rational divisor on Vµ. Consequently D(P) = min y∈∆P (P, y)(h) = γ(P) + L(u)(P) (D.6) is the b-pullback of an effective ample rational divisor D on Vu. (iii) At every actual prime P of Vµ, a minimizer y of (D.5) can be chosen so that e(P, y) is a primitive prime order on X, for some positive integer e. For this choice, a(P) + (P, y)(h) = 1 e , ey ∈ Hom(M, Z). (D.7) On each Vµ, a is the discrepancy function of an effective ordinary lc Calabi–Yau pair, and a + D is that of an effective generalized klt Calabi–Yau pair with nef part D. Each Vµ is of Fano type. At an actual prime outside the floor {a = 0}, the same minimizer satisfies a(P) = 1, e = 1, (P, y)(h) = 0. (D.8)
